reasoning: Glycolysis is essential for glucose catabolism, the primary carbon source.
Core glycolysis (3-carbon phase) is essential under glucose growth.
Gluconeogenesis is repressed when glucose is the carbon source.
PPP provides NADPH and precursors (ribose-5P, erythrose-4P) needed for nucleotide/amino acid/cofactor biosynthesis even when end products are supplied.
PRPP is required for de novo biosynthesis of histidine, nucleotides, NAD, and tryptophan precursors; still needed despite supplementation.
Oxidative PPP is main NADPH source for biosynthesis.
Non-oxidative PPP generates ribose-5P and erythrose-4P required for cofactor/nucleotide backbones.
Entner-Doudoroff pathway is not significantly used for glucose in E. coli; it is induced on gluconate/glucuronate.
TCA cycle is active aerobically for energy generation and biosynthetic precursors.
First half of TCA cycle active for 2-oxoglutarate production (though glutamate is supplied, flux still occurs).
Second half of TCA cycle active under aerobic respiration.
Glyoxylate cycle is repressed in presence of glucose; only active on C2 compounds like acetate.
Proline biosynthesis is repressed by supplied proline in the medium.
Lysine biosynthesis is repressed when lysine is supplied.
Methionine biosynthesis is repressed by supplied methionine.
Threonine biosynthesis is repressed by supplied threonine.
Valine/isoleucine biosynthesis is repressed by supplied BCAAs.
Serine biosynthesis is repressed by supplied serine (present at high concentration).
Cysteine biosynthesis is repressed by supplied cysteine.
Shikimate pathway produces chorismate, needed for menaquinone, ubiquinone, folate, and enterobactin biosynthesis even when aromatic amino acids are supplied; likely reduced flux but not fully off.
Tryptophan biosynthesis is repressed by supplied tryptophan.
Phenylalanine biosynthesis is repressed by supplied phenylalanine.
Tyrosine biosynthesis is repressed by supplied tyrosine.
Histidine biosynthesis is repressed by supplied histidine.
GABA shunt is induced under acid stress/nitrogen limitation; not active under balanced rich growth at neutral pH.
Ornithine biosynthesis is repressed by supplied arginine (via ArgR regulon).

ACGU supplementation provides nucleobases, but de novo purine synthesis is only partially repressed since salvage may not fully meet demand; PurR regulon shows some repression but flux typically continues.
Conversion of IMP to ADP/ATP is essential; adenine salvage also feeds into this but these enzymes remain active.
IMP to GDP/GTP conversion is essential; guanine salvage supplements but enzymes remain active.
Pyrimidine supplementation (uracil, cytosine) represses de novo synthesis via PyrR/attenuation, but some flux typically remains.
UMP to UDP/UTP/CDP/CTP conversion is essential regardless of uracil supply.
Deoxyribonucleotide biosynthesis is essential for DNA replication during growth.
KDO2-lipid A biosynthesis is essential for outer membrane LPS during growth.
Glucuronate degradation is induced only when glucuronate is present; glucose causes catabolite repression.
CMP-KDO biosynthesis is essential for LPS assembly.
ADP-heptose biosynthesis is essential for LPS inner core.
Fatty acid biosynthesis initiation is essential for membrane lipid synthesis.
Fatty acid elongation is essential for membrane lipid synthesis.
Beta-oxidation (acyl-CoA synthesis via FadD) is repressed by glucose/FadR; no fatty acids in medium.
Beta-oxidation is repressed in glucose-replete, fatty acid-absent conditions.
PE biosynthesis is essential; PE is the major E. coli membrane phospholipid.
MEP/non-mevalonate pathway produces IPP/DMAPP, essential for quinone, undecaprenyl-P, and tRNA modification.
NAD biosynthesis is essential; NAD is not supplied in the medium.
Menaquinone is used anaerobically/microaerobically; under aerobic rich growth it is synthesized at lower levels but still produced.
Ubiquinone is the main aerobic respiratory quinone and is essential; not supplied in medium.
Glutathione biosynthesis is active; GSH is not supplied and is essential for redox balance.
Pantothenate is supplied in VA vitamin solution, so biosynthesis is likely repressed/reduced, though no strict repression mechanism; salvage may dominate.
CoA biosynthesis from pantothenate is essential and not bypassed; pantothenate is supplied as precursor.
Heme biosynthesis is essential for cytochromes in aerobic respiration; not supplied in medium.
Biotin biosynthesis is active; biotin is not supplied in VA vitamin mix.
PLP biosynthesis is active; pyridoxal/pyridoxine is not in VA vitamin mix.
Riboflavin/FMN/FAD biosynthesis is active; riboflavin is not supplied.
THF biosynthesis is active; folate is not supplied (PABA is a precursor that is supplied, but downstream synthesis continues).
Thiamine is supplied (thiamine HCl in VA mix); de novo biosynthesis is likely downregulated via TPP riboswitches, but some steps may remain.
Polyamine biosynthesis is essential for growth; spermidine/putrescine not supplied.
Putrescine catabolism to GABA is typically induced on putrescine as N-source; glucose/ammonium conditions repress it.
NADH:quinone oxidoreductase (Complex I/NDH-II) is active during aerobic respiration.
Succinate dehydrogenase is active aerobically as part of TCA cycle and respiration.
Fumarate reductase is expressed anaerobically; repressed under aerobic conditions.
Cytochrome bd is expressed at low O2; under aerobic shaking culture cytochrome bo is dominant, but bd is still present at some level.
F-type ATPase is essential for ATP synthesis via proton motive force.
CAM is a plant pathway annotation; not relevant/active in E. coli.
Assimilatory sulfate reduction is repressed when cysteine is supplied (CysB regulon).
Pyruvate dehydrogenase complex is essential for acetyl-CoA production under aerobic growth.
C10-C20 isoprenoid biosynthesis produces undecaprenyl-PP and quinone precursors, essential for cell wall and respiration.
Cytochrome bo ubiquinol oxidase is the main terminal oxidase under high O2 aerobic growth.
Leucine biosynthesis is repressed by supplied leucine.
Dissimilatory nitrate reduction requires anaerobic conditions and nitrate; not applicable in aerobic rich medium without nitrate.
Trans-cinnamate/3-HPP degradation is induced by substrate; not present in medium and repressed by glucose.
UDP-Glc biosynthesis is needed for LPS, glycogen, and cell wall precursors.
Ascorbate degradation is induced only on ascorbate; not in medium.
Galactonate degradation requires galactonate substrate; not present.
Gal utilization via UDP-Gal is induced by galactose; glucose represses gal operon.
Choline-to-betaine requires choline and osmotic stress; not present and not osmotically stressed.
Isoleucine biosynthesis from threonine is repressed by supplied isoleucine.
Pimeloyl-ACP biosynthesis is active as part of biotin synthesis (biotin not supplied).
Pta-AckA pathway is active during rapid glucose growth causing acetate overflow ('acetate switch').
Glycine cleavage system provides one-carbon units (5,10-methylene-THF) needed for biosynthesis; active during growth.
Galacturonate degradation requires galacturonate; not present and glucose represses.
Galactose Leloir pathway repressed by glucose catabolite repression; no galactose in medium.
Und-P-Ara4N biosynthesis is induced by PhoPQ/PmrAB signaling (cationic AMP, low Mg2+); not triggered in standard rich medium.
dTDP-L-Rha is used for O-antigen in some E. coli strains; K-12 lab strains (MG1655/DH10B) have disrupted O-antigen, so activity depends on strain.
Arginine biosynthesis from ornithine is repressed by supplied arginine (ArgR).
Siroheme is required for sulfite/nitrite reductase cofactor and is synthesized during growth.
Glycogen synthesis occurs mainly in stationary phase or under carbon excess/N-limitation; in exponential rich growth it is low but not zero.
Glycogen degradation occurs upon carbon starvation; not active in glucose-replete growth.
Phenylacetate degradation is induced by phenylacetate; not present and repressed by glucose.
Arginine succinyltransferase pathway is induced when arginine is a N-source; under NH4+ + glucose replete conditions it is repressed.
Molybdenum cofactor is needed for multiple enzymes; synthesized constitutively during growth.
Lipoic acid biosynthesis is essential for PDH/OGDH/GCV complex function; not supplied.
Thiamine salvage from HMP/HET is only relevant if those precursors are present; thiamine itself is supplied so salvage flux is minimal.
UDP-GlcNAc is essential for peptidoglycan and LPS; biosynthesis is active.
dTTP biosynthesis is essential for DNA synthesis during growth.
Pyrimidine degradation (Rut pathway) is induced under N-limitation with pyrimidines as N-source; repressed with NH4+.
Lysine degradation (CadA/LdcC) is induced under low pH or specific conditions; not active in neutral rich medium with lysine supplied as amino acid.
AMP to urate degradation is not a major flux during balanced growth with adenine supplied for salvage.
GMP to urate degradation is not significantly active during balanced growth.
Proline degradation (PutA) is induced by proline as C/N source; with glucose and NH4+ it is repressed despite proline presence.
Methylcitrate cycle is for propionate catabolism; propionate not in medium.
PreQ1 biosynthesis is needed for tRNA queuosine modification; active during growth.
O2-independent ubiquinone biosynthesis (UbiU/V/T) operates anaerobically; under aerobic growth the O2-dependent route (M00117) is used.
UDP-MurNAc is essential for peptidoglycan biosynthesis during growth.
GDP-Man is precursor to GDP-L-Fuc and colanic acid; generally active, though colanic acid is induced under stress.
UDP-Galf is used in some E. coli cell surface glycans; expression depends on strain and conditions.
UDP-ManNAcA is required for enterobacterial common antigen (ECA) biosynthesis, constitutive in E. coli.
GDP-L-Fuc is used for colanic acid capsule; induced under stress (low temp, osmotic); low baseline activity in rich medium.
dTDP-D-Fuc4NAc is used for ECA biosynthesis, constitutively produced.
Sulfoquinovose degradation is induced on SQ as C-source; glucose represses this pathway.
